plan.notes: This plan uses the pantry items early in the week: white rice on day 1, chicken thighs on day 1, and broccoli on day 4. It keeps protein high each day by pairing at least one substantial chicken- or egg-based meal with other balanced meals, while mixing cuisines across the week for variety.

This plan uses the pantry ingredients tofu and kale early in the week, and tempeh is not available in the candidate lists so the rest of the week leans on other vegan proteins. It keeps meals varied across cuisines while emphasizing higher-protein tofu dishes to support the daily protein target alongside roughly calorie-appropriate portions.

This plan keeps the Greek and Indian preferences prominent while using the pantry items chickpeas, feta, and spinach early in the week. The only change boosts day 5 protein by swapping in a higher-protein dinner while preserving the overall 7-day structure and variety.

This plan uses the pantry early with salmon and egg on day 1 and sweet potato on day 2, then keeps the week varied across cuisines and main proteins. Most days land near the energy target with balanced protein from salmon, eggs, chicken, tuna, and legumes, while keeping repeated recipes to a minimum.

This plan keeps the Mexican dishes front and center while using the pantry items early in the week through avocado, black beans, and corn tortillas. The meals stay anchored by higher-protein lunches and dinners to support the 2000 kcal and 85 g protein daily target.

This plan keeps the courgette dish early in the week and uses the chicken-based pantry recipes across several days. It also swaps in lower-carb, high-protein meals to stay close to the calorie target while keeping daily carbs under the limit.

The first day uses the pantry items immediately with cherry tomato, cod, and olives, then the rest of the week keeps leaning on Greek, Italian, and Spanish dishes. The menu emphasizes higher-protein seafood and egg-based meals so the days can be portioned to land near the 2000 kcal target while staying comfortably above 90 g protein.

This plan uses spinach, canned tomatoes, and pasta early in the week, then keeps meals simple with quick mix-and-match recipes. It stays varied across cuisines while leaning on a few higher-energy lunches and dinners to help reach the daily target.

This plan leans on higher-protein lunches and dinners to stay close to the 2000 kcal target while keeping daily carbs balanced. It uses the pantry items early in the week through the pork and red pepper dishes, and it favors Thai, Vietnamese, and nearby flavor profiles where available.

This plan uses the pantry items across the week with beef mince, Greek yogurt, and rolled oats showing up early and repeatedly in different meals. It keeps protein high each day by leaning on the higher-protein mains and snacks while still giving good calorie coverage for the 3000 kcal target.

This plan keeps the original structure where possible while boosting the lower-protein days with more protein-dense meals. It also uses the pantry items early in the week, including egg on day 1 and green beans in the day 1 lunch.

This week uses the pantry early and across multiple meals: spinach, egg, tuna, chicken thigh, leek, butternut squash, red lentils, mushroom, potato, and cheddar all appear by midweek. The plan keeps protein strong with chicken, tuna, eggs, and lentils while mixing lighter and richer meals so daily energy stays near target.

This plan uses the pantry items right away on day 1 and then spreads out the remaining meals with a strong mix of British, French, and American options. Each day lands comfortably around the calorie target while keeping protein well above 80 g, with most dinners and several lunches doing the heavy lifting.

This week uses chickpeas, coconut milk, and quinoa early in the plan, while keeping meals varied across cuisines and main ingredients. The combinations lean on higher-protein lunches and dinners so each day can land near the calorie target and clear the protein goal.

This plan uses the chilli, lime, and prawns right at the start of the week and leans into Thai, Korean, and Mexican flavors throughout. It keeps daily calories in a solid range while prioritizing high-protein lunches and dinners to stay above the protein target.

This plan uses lamb shoulder on day 1 and couscous on day 2, while leaning into Moroccan and Middle Eastern flavors throughout. The meals are varied in proteins and keep each day in a reasonable calorie range for the 1500 kcal target.
